name: Example: Computing the Integral of a Trigonometric Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
worked_solution:
In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2} & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2})(\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))-\int (\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{3}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\displaystyle \int x\sin(3x) \textrm{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x=-\,\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =x(-\,\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))-\int (-\,\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))\cdot 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{3}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x \\  & =-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{3}(\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))+{C}_{1} \\  & =-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{9}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+{C}_{1}\,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C_1$ is a constant of integration.
So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{3}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{3}(-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{9}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+{C}_{1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{2}{9}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{27}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2{C}_{1}}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{27}((9{x}^{2}-2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C = -\dfrac{2C_1}{3}.$
